extracted.intended_audience: patent practitioners (attorneys and agents) who file/oppose motions in AIA (PTAB) proceedings
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for requesting authorization, drafting, timing, page limits, and content of motions in AIA (PTAB) trials (IPR/CBM/PGR), plus standards for common motions (pro hac vice, supplemental information, joinder, seal, exclude, discovery, terminate).

rubrics_metrics.name: General considerations for authorizing/granting motions
rubrics_metrics.description: In addition to the merits, the Board may consider burden on parties; efficient, effective resolution of issues; documenting for due process and Administrative Procedure Act; statutory deadlines; effect on schedule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These considerations inform whether the Board will authorize a motion or grant requested relief; weight given to schedule efficiency and administrative burden may outweigh other factors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requesting authorization procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: Authorization obtained via conference call with panel; common procedure – request by email (should copy all parties; indicate generally the relief requested or subject matter of the call; should not include substantive argument or attachments (e.g., draft motions); should include multiple times when all parties are available; should state any opposition and address the meet & confer requirement).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not include draft motions or substantive attachments in authorization request emails; include multiple availability times; copying all parties and stating any opposition/meet-and-confer attempts expedites authorization requests and avoids procedural defects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Burden of proof for motions
rubrics_metrics.description: Burden of proof to establish entitlement to requested relief is on the moving party: § 42.20(c).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Moving party must show by the applicable standard that relief is warranted; prepare factual and legal showings accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Content requirements for motions (§ 42.22)
rubrics_metrics.description: Motions are filed as a separate paper per § 42.22 and must include a statement of precise relief requested and a full statement of reasons for request, including detailed explanation of significance of evidence, material facts, and law. All showings required by rules must be included. Oppositions and replies governed by § 42.23. Identify any disputed material facts to avoid unintentional admission; replies directed only to corresponding opposition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Draft motions to stand alone as a separate paper with clear requested relief and comprehensive reasons; explicitly identify disputed facts; limit replies to issues raised in the corresponding opposition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Page limits for motions and responses (§ 42.24)
rubrics_metrics.description: Motions - 15 pages: § 42.24(a)(1)(v). Unless waiver granted in advance: § 42.24(a)(2). Oppositions - same number of pages as corresponding motion: § 42.24(b)(3). Replies to motions - 5 pages: § 42.24(c)(2). Limits INCLUDE any statement of material facts to be admitted or denied: § 42.24(a)(1). Limits EXCLUDE table of contents, certificate of service, appendix of exhibits: § 42.24(a)(1). The Board may set other page constraints (e.g., fewer pages when granting authorization to file).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Count pages carefully; include statements of material facts in page count; rely on exclusions (TOC, certificate, appendix) appropriately; seek advance waiver if more pages needed and anticipate Board-imposed shorter limits when authorization is granted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing for filing motions
rubrics_metrics.description: Deadlines for filing motions are set in the Scheduling Order. Specific items (e.g., patent owner motion to amend, motions to exclude) have timing slots. Opposition default – 1 month: § 42.25(a)(1), but scheduling orders typically set much shorter times. The Board can deny relief not promptly sought: § 42.25(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check the Scheduling Order for exact due dates; do not assume default timelines; file promptly or risk denial as untimely.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pro hac vice motions (37 C.F.R. § 42.10)
rubrics_metrics.description: Pro hac vice admission authorized in Notice of Filing Date; no sooner than 21 days after service of petition. Oppose within 1 week; no reply to opposition unless Board authorizes. Motion must show counsel has sufficient legal and technical qualifications, established familiarity with subject matter, and party intends to be represented by attorney. Motion must be accompanied by an affidavit of counsel seeking pro hac vice admission (required affidavit contents (8 items)). Needed when attorney not registered to practice at USPTO; eligible only as back-up counsel; may not withdraw without Board authorization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare the required affidavit (including the eight specified items) and demonstrate technical/legal qualifications and familiarity. Use pro hac vice for back-up counsel only and note that withdrawal requires Board authorization; monitor the short opposition window.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplemental information vs supplemental evidence (37 C.F.R. § 42.64(b)(2) and § 42.123)
rubrics_metrics.description: "Supplemental information" is different than "supplemental evidence". Only supplemental information requires an authorized motion. "Supplemental evidence—served in response to an evidentiary objection and filed in response to a motion to exclude—is offered solely to support admissibility of the originally filed evidence and to defeat a motion to exclude that evidence, and not to support any argument on the merits. Supplemental information is evidence a party intends to support an argument on the merits and may only be filed if a § 123 motion is both authorized and granted." (Handi Quilter, Inc. v. Bernina Int’l AG, IPR2013-00364, Paper 30.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If evidence is intended to bolster admissibility after an objection, treat as supplemental evidence (no authorization). If evidence will be used on the merits, seek authorization under § 42.123 — include the required showings and timing rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Motion to submit supplemental information criteria (37 C.F.R. §§ 42.123, 223)
rubrics_metrics.description: Authorization to file is required. Motion must be filed within 1 month of instituting trial. The supplemental information must be relevant to a claim on which trial was instituted (not the grounds). If filed more than 1 month after institution, must show (1) why the information could not reasonably have been obtained earlier; and (2) why filing in the interests of justice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Motions are not automatic even if criteria met; the Board will consider efficient administration and completing IPR on time. Do not include the exhibit itself in the motion — submit the exhibit only if the motion is granted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Motion for joinder (37 C.F.R. §§ 42.122, 222)
rubrics_metrics.description: Motion for joinder must be filed no later than 1 month after institution date. A request for authorization to file the joinder motion is not required. The Board considers the impact on schedule/efficiency and whether it can avoid major changes to the scheduling order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The joinder motion should provide reasons why joinder is appropriate, explain any impact on schedule and costs, address how briefing/discovery can be simplified (e.g., consolidated filings), limit separate filings to the joined party’s disagreements, and request consolidated depositions (with no extension of allotted time unless authorized).

rubrics_metrics.name: Motion to seal (37 C.F.R. §§ 42.14, 54)
rubrics_metrics.description: Motions to seal are for confidential information only — public policy favors making information available. Standard = good cause. Motion must include a proposed protective order (if one has not already been entered) — Board’s default protective order is NOT automatically entered (entry must be requested) — and show differences from Board’s default order. Motion must include certification that moving party attempted/conferred in good faith with opposing party on scope of order and an explanation of why info is confidential.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Production of same information in district court as confidential alone is not good cause but provides context. Information likely not confidential if previously publicly available. For irrelevant personal information consider redactions (e.g., account numbers). Consider moving to expunge confidential information after final judgment (37 C.F.R. § 42.56).

rubrics_metrics.name: Motions to exclude evidence (37 C.F.R. § 42.62; § 42.64)
rubrics_metrics.description: Federal Rules of Evidence generally apply to proceedings: § 42.62. Objections prior to institution typically are premature; they are addressed during trial (e.g., lack of authentication). Objections are required. Objections to be filed within 10 business days of institution of trial to evidence submitted during preliminary phase: § 42.64(b)(1). During trial – file objection within 5 business days of service: § 42.64(b)(1). Respond by serving supplemental evidence within 10 business days of objection: § 42.64(b)(2). Objections themselves are not motions to exclude. A motion to exclude is required to preserve an objection: § 42.64(c) — due date set in Scheduling Order. Identify grounds with sufficient particularity to allow correction with supplemental evidence (e.g., authentication by testimony). If party objects after supplementation, that party moves to exclude.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow objection deadlines strictly; use supplementation deadlines to cure admissibility issues; file a motion to exclude to preserve objections when required by scheduling order.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contents and limits of a motion to exclude
rubrics_metrics.description: Motion to exclude must identify each objection in the record and where the evidence sought to be excluded was relied upon; explain each objection (may include exhibits to the motion) — explain why the information/evidence is not admissible. A motion to exclude is NOT a substantive sur-reply, NOT a vehicle to challenge sufficiency of evidence to prove a fact, and NOT a vehicle to argue whether a reply or supporting evidence is of appropriate scope (Conopco, Inc. v. Procter & Gamble Co., IPR2013-00505).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Limit the motion to admissibility grounds and identification of the challenged evidence; avoid using the motion to litigate the merits or to reargue sufficiency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Motions for additional discovery (37 C.F.R. § 42.51)
rubrics_metrics.description: Authorization to file is required. Consideration is case specific. Parties may agree to additional discovery between themselves. Content of motion should address Garmin factors concerning whether additional discovery is in the interests of justice (see IPR2012-00001, Paper 26 for IPR): 1) More than a possibility and mere allegation; 2) Litigation positions and underlying basis; 3) Ability to generate equivalent information by other means; 4) Easily understandable instructions; 5) Requests not overly burdensome to answer. See also Bloomberg Inc. v. Markets-Alert Pty Ltd., Case CBM2013-00005, Paper 32 for CBM and PGR (good cause).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tailor requests to Garmin factors; demonstrate specificity, relevance, and that requested discovery is necessary and not obtainable by other means; show requests are not overly burdensome and supply clear instructions for discovery.

rubrics_metrics.name: Motion to terminate and settlements (37 C.F.R. §§ 42.72–42.74; 35 U.S.C. §§ 317, 327)
rubrics_metrics.description: Termination: § 42.72 covers termination of a party (Board may proceed to final written decision even if no petitioner remains) and termination of the proceeding (Board enters judgment). A party may request adverse judgment: § 42.73(b). Disclaimer of patent, claim cancellation, concession of unpatentability, and abandonment of contest may be construed as such a request. Parties can settle any issue via joint request: 35 U.S.C. § 317(a), § 327(a). All agreements/understandings must be in writing & filed with the Board; no side agreements (panel may require parties to represent that no side agreements exist in the motion). Settlement materials may be treated as business confidential — request to keep separate. The Board is not a party to the settlement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: File joint requests for settlement with full disclosure and required filings; do not rely on side agreements; consider business confidential handling and possible expungement or special treatment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Estoppel under 35 U.S.C. § 315(e)(1)
rubrics_metrics.description: (e) Estoppel. — (1) Proceedings before the office.—The petitioner in an inter partes review of a claim . . . that results in a final written decision . . . may not request or maintain a proceeding before the Office with respect to that claim on any ground that the petitioner raised or reasonably could have raised during that inter partes review. 35 U.S.C. § 315(e)(1); see 37 C.F.R. § 42.73(d). Termination: Of a second proceeding – Board enters judgment in a first proceeding and terminates a second proceeding (no joinder) having a ground that reasonably could have been raised in first proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be mindful that claims and grounds litigated (or reasonably raisable) in a prior final IPR can estop later PTO proceedings; consider estoppel implications when deciding whether to assert grounds or join proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authorization and filing practice notes
rubrics_metrics.description: Common practical guidance: authorization requests should not include substantive attachments or draft motions; motions must be filed as separate papers; Board may impose shorter page limits when granting authorization; some motions require authorization to file (listed in appendix table).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the Board's procedural expectations when requesting authorization and filing motions; consult the Trial Practice Guide and the Scheduling Order; anticipate Board-specific page and timing adjustments.
